# 3.2.x Vulcanus discovery recovery preparation

This disposable three-stage fixture keeps the single `mir-fixture-discovery-recovery` identity while a published MIR 3.2.0 or 3.2.1 source save is handed to MIR5 on official Factorio 2.1.23 Space Age. The source validates the emitted historical iron row, including its exact unordered `iron-plate` and `casting-iron` productivity vector, and the native `planet-discovery-vulcanus` `unlock-travel-to-space-platforms` effect. It retains that source iron formula and time unchanged, accelerating only the source discovery lab. The MIR5 successor validates its current iron row and accelerates only that candidate lab to one count and five seconds. It labels only direct prerequisite seeds, requires the real source discovery to be researched while Vulcanus remains natively locked, then scripts the independent MIR iron level-three/42-percent queue witness. It does not insert an unlock effect or call `lock_space_location` to manufacture that source state. Those scripted iron values are fixture state, not published defaults or an observation of the historical defect.

The source also creates a separate foreign force with unresearched locked Vulcanus and a 27-percent iron queue. The MIR5 successor never unlocks a location itself: before it creates a laboratory or writes successor storage, it requires the ordinary MIR recovery to have restored only the researched player location while preserving the foreign lock, both iron queues, the player level-three 20-percent iron-plate contribution, saved-progress domain/value, and the protected same-mod fixture state. It then proves supplied science was consumed by one current iron laboratory, saves, and requires two read-only cold reload observations.

The 3.2.0 wrapper deliberately refuses if its actual emitted `planet-discovery-vulcanus` row is absent. Historical evidence records that a 3.2.0 external discovery target could be pruned; this fixture never recreates, unhides, or substitutes that prototype to force an input through. The 3.2.1 route is likewise only prepared source input until its exact package, engine execution, source save, successor run, and two reloads are independently captured.

Each stage is a five-member caller-composed fixture projection: the stage `info.json`, `control.lua`, and `data-final-fixes.lua`, plus the shared `fixture_control.lua` and `fixture_data_final.lua`. The [prepared input record](../../../spec/evidence/discovery-recovery-prepared-inputs-r02.json) pins the reviewed raw source, owned archives, eight-mod selections and a private proposed-helper package. Its separate a575 control observes whether the engine itself restores discovery; a control pass cannot establish that the helper ran or was necessary. Source-save hashes remain unbound, and Black Glass retains native scheduling and exclusive library ownership. This preparation does not qualify a full 3.2 catalogue, ordinary science tuning, historical bug cause, performance, Library behavior, multiplayer, or release readiness.
